parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argv, PBKDF2 output, /output delivery, no Python embedding, and no pbkdf2 helper requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but also spawned CLI and algorithm probes that were able to act in the shared /output workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a pure JavaScript SHA-1, HMAC-SHA1, PBKDF2, byte utility, CLI parser, and test7.mjs, while one child wrote an alternate implementation tree.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final delivered tree combined parent modules with child-origin modules after the parent noticed the alternate output and reconciled shared byte exports.
parallel.verification: The parent checked sample vectors, Unicode input, several parser edge cases, and module import consistency before the final answer.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 34 of 70 cases, and the parallel process left evidence of a mixed-provenance output tree caused by concurrent child writes.

serial.requirements: The single agent recognized ESM, .mjs output, manual argv parsing, local module organization, and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run had one owner for probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery, with no child handoffs or shared writer conflict.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote test7.mjs, argparse.mjs, and crypto helper modules using a Node createHmac wrapper to implement PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial tree was produced in one patch under /output/lib/crypto and /output/lib/cli and then delivered as a coherent file set.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran direct sample checks and a normalized multi-case comparison that ended with MATCHED before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 34 of 70 cases, so the one-agent implementation also left hidden acceptance obligations unmet despite local checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the need for Node ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior, and /output placement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same requirements and probed executable behavior before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap explains the equal official failure; both missed some hidden acceptance cases despite covering the visible prompt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split probing and implementation across parent, CLI child, algorithm child, and a nested algorithm child, but write ownership of /output was not isolated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one actor responsible for behavior probing, implementation, tests, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader concurrent ownership and a shared-output conflict; serial had simpler ownership and no delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received enough task context to probe behavior, but the run lacked a clear shared-file ownership contract for the deliverable tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent context boundary and kept all interface decisions inside one implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context/interface difference is not missing task facts; it is the parallel shared workspace boundary that allowed incompatible implementations to meet at /output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a pure-JS SHA-1/HMAC/PBKDF2 implementation and later kept extra child-origin PBKDF2/index modules in the final artifact list.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a Node built-in HMAC helper module plus PBKDF2 block assembly and a manual argparse-like parser.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The algorithms were behaviorally similar on visible tests, but parallel had mixed parent/child module provenance whereas serial had one implementation lineage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited briefly, then interrupted direct child agents; the nested algorithm result was visible by a later list_agents call, but the CLI child had no final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and completed its own verification before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result lifecycle churn, but parent took over and delivered; serial avoided that coordination surface entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel explicitly observed an alternate /output implementation written by a concurrent child and fixed a byte helper export mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent output tree in a single patch and had no concurrent workspace writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered a shared-state collision with a realized reconciliation cost; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel checked samples, Unicode, CLI edge cases, and module consistency, then official evaluation failed 36/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial checked samples and ran a normalized multi-case comparison that printed MATCHED, then official evaluation also failed 36/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had cleaner pre-final verification evidence, but both local verification suites missed the same scale of official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel took 370 agent seconds, issued many tool calls, interrupted children, reconciled output consistency, and finalized before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial took 271 agent seconds, no subagents, fewer tool calls, and finalized before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget and closure effort on coordination cleanup, but neither run timed out and both had the same official score.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records show both parallel and serial failed with the same 36/70 result, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. Both attempts implemented PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 and manual CLI handling and passed visible local checks. The concrete difference is process-level: parallel had a shared-output overwrite and cleanup episode, while serial stayed single-owner. The equal official score means that episode is retained as a realized parallel-side adverse coordination pattern, not as the proven reason for an outcome split.
parallel_contributors: Parallel parent and child wrote overlapping /output deliverables and the parent then reconciled mixed modules.
Parallel verified samples and several CLI cases but still failed hidden official cases.
serial_contributors: Serial produced one cohesive output tree without child writes.
Serial also verified visible cases and still failed hidden official cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial used node:crypto createHmac while parallel's parent implementation used a handwritten SHA-1/HMAC path, but both reached the same official score.
Both implementations accepted the program-name difference in help/error output as expected basename behavior, which may have contributed to failed hidden CLI comparisons.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process pattern, no official outcome difference
